prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map clearly separates the multi-level brick construction site into distinct distance tiers: the foreground brick ledge (~0.5–1.2 m in front of and below the camera wearer) and the adjacent vertical brick wall on the left in frames 3–5 (~0.3–0.8 m away, within arm's reach) appear bright white, contrasting with the mid-ground bamboo scaffolding poles (~1.5–2 m below), the lower brick enclosure (~3 m below), and the open ground rendered pitch black (~4–6 m below). In frames 1–2, another worker stands ~1.5–2 m away to the right and slightly below the camera wearer, facing left toward the brick ledge with his torso and outstretched right arm (~1.2–1.5 m away) rendered in mid-grey, before the camera wearer turns left in frames 3–5, moving that worker out of view and bringing the wearer's own left hand (~0.4–0.6 m away) into the lower-left foreground to hold a horizontal guide string against the wall corner. This map makes the steep vertical drop to the ground and the sharp 90-degree corner geometry between the left wall and front brick course immediately quantifiable compared to the sunlit RGB textures. However, it is unreliable around fine structures and low-contrast boundaries, blending the other worker's shoulder and head into the right-hand brick wall in frame 1 and merging the suspended guide string into the darker background depth in frames 4–5 despite capturing it as a faint bright line in frames 2–3.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is completely blank (solid black) across all five frames, failing to detect any people or objects in the scene. From the RGB strip, the scene actually contains another worker ~1.5–2 m to the right in frames 1–2 (who becomes increasingly occluded by the right frame edge in frame 2 and leaves the field of view as the camera wearer turns left in frames 3–5), as well as the camera wearer's own left hand (~0.4–0.6 m away, within arm's reach of the brick corner) and sandals resting on bamboo scaffolding (~1.5 m below the camera) in frames 3–5. Because no masks or class labels are generated, the segmentation map provides no spatial information beyond the RGB image and is entirely unreliable under this steep downward egocentric viewing angle and harsh lighting.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely blank across frames 1, 3, 4, and 5, detecting only a single magenta right-hand skeleton in frame 2 located to the right of the foreground brick ledge at roughly 1.2–1.5 m from the camera wearer. That detected hand belongs to the other worker standing ~1.5–2 m away on the right and shows his fingers pinched forward toward the top edge of the bricks within his arm's reach, just before the camera wearer turns left and rotates him out of view in frame 3. While this single detection confirms the exact articulation and orientation of the worker's right hand in the shaded gap beside the wall—which is dark and hard to resolve in the RGB frame—the map is otherwise highly unreliable. It completely misses the worker's yellow body skeleton and left arm in frames 1–2 (where his head and torso face left toward the wall and slightly toward the camera wearer) as well as the camera wearer's own reaching left hand (~0.4–0.6 m away) and feet (~1.5 m below) in frames 3–5.
